summary: Security-remediation backend verification for CloudBite. Wrote a fresh pytest suite that creates its own admin/manager/customer/delivery-partner accounts (since demo seed users were removed) and validates all four SEC-* fixes plus JWT hardening and regression flows. 27/27 tests passed in ~11s.
critical_code_review_comments: SEC-001: /api/auth/forgot-password stores sha256(token_hash), never returns the raw token, and logs only the email — good. Reset endpoint hashes the incoming token and matches by token_hash; returns 400 for invalid/expired/used tokens. Verified.

SEC-002: utils.safe_regex uses re.escape and 100-char cap; wired into routes_menu.list_menu, routes_orders.list_orders (q), routes_admin.list_customers (q). Malicious patterns like (a+)+$, .*, a{99999} all return in <3s with 200. Verified.

SEC-003: routes_delivery._get_active_assignment(expected=[...]) enforces state machine — accept requires 'assigned', pickup requires 'accepted', start requires 'picked_up', delivered requires 'out_for_delivery'. Illegal steps 400 with 'Invalid delivery step...'. payment_status='paid' only set inside mark_delivered after out_for_delivery gate. Verified.

SEC-004: routes_misc.mark_read wraps ObjectId in try/except (400 on malformed) and applies owner-scoped filter (user_id=user.id OR role_target='staff' for staff). Cross-user mark-read is a genuine no-op — verified by comparing admin's notification 'read' state before/after the customer's attempt. Verified.
JWT hardening: auth.get_current_user now rejects tokens whose payload 'type' != 'access'. Confirmed by minting a valid HS256 token with type='refresh' using the server's JWT_SECRET and receiving 401.

Minor observation (not a blocker): reset-password with empty string token currently returns 400 (hash of empty string doesn't match any record) — Pydantic doesn't min-length validate. Fine, but consider adding min_length=1 to ResetPasswordReq.token for defense-in-depth.

Minor observation: /api/notifications/{nid}/read returns generic {"message":"ok"} even when the update matched 0 documents. Behaviour matches the security intent (no info leak) but you might want to log/audit unauthorized attempts.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (rewritten — creates own accounts, covers SEC-001..004, JWT hardening, regression)
test_credentials: Admin hungrypot457@gmail.com/Admin@12345 (seeded). Manager/customer/delivery accounts are created dynamically per session inside the pytest fixtures (TEST_* prefix).
seed_data_creation: Each test session creates: 1 customer (register), 1 manager (POST /api/admin/managers), 1 delivery partner (POST /api/admin/delivery-partners) plus several TEST_ orders across delivery-lifecycle scenarios. Not cleaned up so main agent can inspect audit logs / orders.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py; no seed accounts required beyond the env-seeded admin. Uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. Reads JWT_SECRET from /app/backend/.env for the non-access-type token test (skips if unreadable). All SEC-* fixes verified end-to-end; the only optional hardenings are (a) Pydantic min_length on reset token, (b) auditing unauthorized notification/read attempts.
